issue.title: Executor Estimator: TREX calibration shot budget is mis-sized

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

issue.body:
## Summary

The executor-based `EstimatorV2` sizes the TREX (measure-noise-learning)
calibration item incorrectly. The calibration still returns `evs`, so the
divergence is silent, but the shot cost is wrong.

## Where

- `qiskit_ibm_runtime/executor_estimator/trex_utils.py` (`create_trex_calibration_circuit`)
- `qiskit_ibm_runtime/executor_estimator/prepare.py` (and `prepare_pea` / `prepare_pec` / `prepare_zne`)
- `qiskit_ibm_runtime/options_models/measure_noise_learning_options.py`
  (`shots_per_randomization` default `"auto"`, `num_randomizations` default `32`)

## Problem

A `QuantumProgram` has a single global per-randomization shot budget, shared by
the estimation items and the TREX calibration item, so the TREX item cannot carry
its own `shots_per_randomization`. Today the TREX item just runs
`num_randomizations` (default 32) at that global per-randomization budget. Because
the budget grows ~`1/precision²`, TREX cost grows without bound as precision
tightens (e.g. `program_shots ≈ 10k` → ~320k TREX shots).

## Proposed fix

Keep `shots_per_randomization` at `"auto"` and never resolve it to a concrete
per-randomization value (an explicit int should not be supported — it is being
deprecated). Since the TREX item always runs at the fixed global per-randomization
budget, size the calibration purely by **scaling `num_randomizations`** so the
total TREX shots land at an appropriate, bounded budget instead of
`32 × program_shots`.

issue.title: Executor Sampler: dict-keyed parameter values bind in the wrong order

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

issue.body:
## Summary

The executor-based `SamplerV2` flattens a pub's parameter values to a positional
array **without** passing the circuit's parameter order. For a pub whose values are
given as a dict / `BindingsArray` whose key order differs from the circuit's
canonical `circuit.parameters` order, the values bind to the **wrong parameters** —
silently, with no error and no warning.

## Where

- `qiskit_ibm_runtime/executor_sampler/prepare.py:103` (no-twirl path) and `:137`
  (twirl path) — both call `pub.parameter_values.as_array()`.

## Problem

`BindingsArray.as_array()` called with no argument *"preserves the order of both the
dict and the parameters in the keys"* (qiskit `bindings_array.py:189-194`) — i.e. the
user's dict insertion order. `SamplerPub.coerce` does not re-canonicalize a dict
(`sampler_pub.py:135` → `BindingsArray.coerce(values)`), so the keys stay in user
order.

The resulting `CircuitItem.circuit_arguments` is a bare positional float array with
no parameter names (`quantum_program/quantum_program.py:82-114`), so the executor can
only bind it positionally against the circuit's canonical `circuit.parameters`
(sorted). When the dict order ≠ canonical order, parameters are swapped.

Reproduced offline: circuit with params canonical `[a, b]`, values `{b: 0.0, a: π/2}`
→ wrapper array `[0.0, 1.57]` (dict order b, a) vs correct `[1.57, 0.0]` (canonical
a, b). `a` and `b` are silently swapped.

- **Trigger:** dict / `BindingsArray`-keyed multi-parameter pub with non-canonical key order.
- **Safe:** plain positional-array pubs — `SamplerPub.coerce` wraps them as
  `{tuple(circuit.parameters): values}`, so they're already canonical.
- **Impact:** silent wrong results (no exception). Legacy binds by name → unaffected.

## Fix

Pass the circuit's parameters to `as_array` so the flattened array is ordered
canonically:

```python
# executor_sampler/prepare.py  (both the no-twirl and twirl paths)
param_values = pub.parameter_values.as_array(pub.circuit.parameters)
```

`as_array(parameters)` reorders to the given parameter order (and validates the set
matches), which is exactly the canonical order the positional `circuit_arguments`
axis is bound against.

## Also affects the estimator

The executor **`EstimatorV2`** has the same flaw: `compute_samplex_arguments`
calls `parameter_values.as_array()` with no parameter list
(`executor_estimator/utils.py:390`), feeding all four prepare paths (`prepare.py`,
`prepare_pea.py`, `pec/prepare_pec.py`, `zne/prepare_zne.py`). Same fix — pass the
pub's circuit parameters into `as_array` there too.

comments.body:
Thanks, Leo.
Is this something that the old Sampler used to handle, and that is handled incorrectly by the executor-based Sampler?
If yes, we should let @emilkovacev know, and ask him to add one small test

> Thanks, Leo. Is this something that the old Sampler used to handle, and that is handled incorrectly by the executor-based Sampler? If yes, we should let [@emilkovacev](https://github.com/emilkovacev) know, and ask him to add one small test

Looks like this is a wrapper only issue. The legacy works as intended.

issue.title: Add integration tests for wrapper-estimator

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Exists, but can be done better, faster, or different

issue.body:
**What is the expected feature or enhancement?**

While we have some unit test coverage of the wrapper-estimator internals there is currently no integration test exercising the full functionality of running `WrapperEstimator` jobs.

Similar to #2645 and #2644, we we should have some integration tests capturing the functionality. 

**Acceptance criteria**

At least one integration test that runs a meaningful `WrapperEstimator` job against a device is added.

comments.body:
During a recent meeting with the addons team, it was brought up that we should monitor the RTT (round-trip time) of executor-based estimator (and sampler) jobs, to make sure that we don't take a hit on performance in the future without detecting it. 

RTT is defined as the time between pressing ENTER on `estimator.run(pubs)` to the time that I get `job.result()` back, minus the time spent in the queue and the "quantum" time spent running quantum circuits on the QPU. All these info is available somewhere, likely around the job metrics

I would be curious to know if we can augment the scope of the integration tests to also track RTT, for the reason that:
- Calculating RTT should be pretty straightforward, based on the info above
- We are already submitting jobs, may as well take full advantage of them

Monitoring (i.e., the act of comparing RTT with RTT of previous jobs) seems trickier though, and likely what needs investigation.

Just dropping this here, so that we don't forget

Thanks, and indeed we should not forget about it. One factor at play is integration test total runtime: we do want to keep them within reasonable limits.

This issue was opened with a smaller scope, though: specifically, having at least one integration tests for the estimator in the same spirit as the existing integration tests for Executor and WrapperSampler, so we can detect breakages fast (and have a quick way of testing that the estimator works when developing). By having a minimal test (or small number of them), we gain confidence without significant impact to test time.

Closing via #3189 and #3192.

Will open a separate issue for RTT.

issue.body:
**What is the expected enhancement?**

Historically, we have been using `pydantic.dataclass` as the way to defined Options, with a number of constructs on top of it (with `@primitive_dataclass` + `OptionsV2` as the main driver: a hierarchy of classes, with `arbitrary_types_allowed`, and logic for converting, extracting information, coping with older versions of the options and visualization). For new programs, we have been using `pydantic.dataclass` with a leaner configuration (no hierarchy, explicitly avoiding `Unset` and arbitrary types), which increases explicitness and simplifies implementation.

Arguably, Options are involved in:
* interface design (a way for users to configure the behavior of a program in an ergonomic discoverable way)
* validation (ensure correctness and explicitly declare the allowed values and constrains)
* serialization (used for constructing part of the payload that is sent to the API)

Keeping Options thin and using Pydantic BaseModels seems to naturally provide solutions to those needs, allowing to take advantage of pydantic features fully and remove the need for custom functionality, resulting in more maintainable code and providing more features "for free". This story is about exploring such approach.

**Acceptance criteria**

Using `BaseModels` for `option_models` is explored, and evaluated by the team.

comments.body:
User API changes (for internal tracking):

- [x] Rename `qasm_simulator` to `backend` to match `Executor` (#3079)
- [x] Rename `AerExecutor` and `AerRuntimeJob` to `SimExecutor` and `SimRuntimeJob`, respectively (#3100)

Currently the way to pass a noise map to aer-executor is something like

```python
pm = generate_boxing_passmanager(tags="tag1", inject_noise=True)

samplex_arguments = {"inject_noise_ref1": some_noise_model}
map = {"tag1": another_noise_model}

executor = AerExecutor(backend=AerSimulator(), map)
job = executor.run(program)
```

There was a discussion on why `map` here is specified in `AerExecutor` constructor, when this `map` likely has a strong coupling to the input quantum program. The motivation was to avoid having to change the `run()` method invocation when switching between a simulator and a real QPU. 

This syntax might become a bit of problem when we want to add local mode support for Executor (#3055), which would allow

```python
backend = AerSimulator()
# backend = service.backend("ibm_torino")    # uncomment for real QPU

executor = Executor(backend)
job = executor.run(program)
```

To simplify the future local mode support, I suggest we instead add a `SimulatorOption` option class to Executor. These options are ignored if the backend is not a simulator. This allows one to do

```python
pm = generate_boxing_passmanager(tags="tag1", inject_noise=True)

samplex_arguments = {"inject_noise_ref1": some_noise_model}

# executor = Executor(backend)   # replace next line with this for real QPU
executor = AerExecutor(backend=AerSimulator())
executor.options.simulator.noise_map = {"tag1": another_noise_model}   # ignored if using real QPU
executor.options.simulator.seed_simulator = 123   # ignored if using real QPU

job = executor.run(program)
```

Note that 
1. The example above also has a `seed_simulator` option. Specifying a seed is very common. While that's an argument you can pass to `AerSimulator()`, it's not something you can pass to a fake backend constructor. Although alternatively this can be done using `backend=AerSimulator.from_backend(FakeTorino(), seed_simulator=123)`
2. There is an existing [SimulatorOptions](https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/blob/020b3cbdabaaee50dcb6aa816dfa512d1f1a0ae9/qiskit_ibm_runtime/options_models/simulator.py#L37) class. It was originally created for cloud simulators, and all of the options can already be pass directly to `AerSimulator()`

@jyu00, this makes sense to me at a high level!
Let's explore it, cc @apchytr

issue.title: PEC noise-model recipe errors on the default (or silently wastes QPU)

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

issue.body:
**Component:** `executor_estimator` `EstimatorV2` — building `resilience.noise_model_mapping` via
`find_unique_layers` + `NoiseLearnerV3` + `NoiseLearnerV3Results.to_dict`.

## Symptom

Building a PEC noise-model mapping the documented way — pass `find_unique_layers` output to
`NoiseLearnerV3.run`, then `to_dict` — raises on the default `require_refs=True`:

```
ValueError: Found an instruction without an inject noise annotation.
            Consider setting 'require_refs' to ``False``.
```

Taking that suggestion (`require_refs=False`) makes it run, but the job then spends real QPU
TREX-characterizing a full-width measurement box whose result is discarded — it has no `InjectNoise` ref, so
it can't enter `noise_model_mapping`, and readout mitigation is done by an in-run TREX pass regardless.

## Repro

```python
est = EstimatorV2(mode, options)          # options.resilience.pec_mitigation = True
layers  = est.find_unique_layers(pubs)    # gate layer(s) + an appended measurement box
results = NoiseLearnerV3(mode).run(layers).result()
mapping = results.to_dict(layers)         # <-- raises: measurement box has no InjectNoise ref
```

`find_unique_layers` returns an **extra measurement box** on top of the gate layer(s). Inspecting its output
on Bell/ZZ (`inject_noise` on):

```python
for layer in est.find_unique_layers(pubs):
    ann = get_annotation(layer.operation, InjectNoise)
    print(layer.operation.num_qubits, "ref=", ann.ref if ann else None)
# 2    ref= 'raaaA'   <- gate layer         (InjectNoise; PEC reads this)
# 156  ref= None      <- appended measurement box (no InjectNoise; nothing reads it)
```

The `156` box is the full-width measurement layer the boxing appends for execution — never present in the
user's circuit, and the box `to_dict` raises on.

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** the documented recipe builds the mapping with default settings.
- **Actual:** it raises; the `require_refs=False` workaround succeeds but silently adds a wasted TREX pass to
  every PEC run.

## Likely cause

`find_unique_layers` returns every unique box, including ones with no `InjectNoise` ref: the measurement box
`box_circuit` synthesizes for the *execution* path (estimator pubs carry no measurements), and — depending on
transpilation/twirling — non-injected gate layers too. None are consumed by PEC/PEA: only
`InjectNoise`-annotated layers key into `noise_model_mapping`, `prepare_pec` re-boxes independently
(`prepare_pec.py:128`), and readout is an in-run TREX calibration. So for `inject_noise` runs the recipe
should hand back only the `InjectNoise` layers; any other box is ref-less (→ the `to_dict` raise) and, if
passed to the learner, wasted QPU.

## Impact (measured, ibm_fez, Bell/ZZ)

The wasted TREX pass pushes the wrapper's `run + learn` above legacy inline learning; dropping it brings them
to parity (±~2–4 s job overhead). Largest relative cost on shallow circuits.

issue.title: BlockBasePadder corrupts scheduling metadata for rebuilt control-flow operations

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

`BlockBasePadder` can corrupt scheduling metadata while rebuilding dynamic-circuit control-flow operations. A scheduled control-flow node's block index is overwritten by the loop index used to traverse its bodies, and recursive `_visit_block()` calls do not restore the parent's `_idle_after` or `_current_block_idx`. The final fast-path barrier call also passes `(time, block_idx)` where the method expects `(block_idx, time)`.

Together these defects can make padding change `property_set["node_start_time"]`, leak nested timing state into the parent traversal, and attach barriers to the wrong block/time.

This is the focused subset of #3005 addressed by #3076. The separate idle-qubit detection problem described in #3005 is not part of this report.

**Steps to reproduce**

Run the following against current `main`:

```python
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.circuit import ControlFlowOp
from qiskit.circuit.library import Measure, XGate
from qiskit.transpiler.passmanager import PassManager
from qiskit.transpiler.target import InstructionProperties, Target

from qiskit_ibm_runtime.transpiler.passes.scheduling.pad_delay import PadDelay
from qiskit_ibm_runtime.transpiler.passes.scheduling.scheduler import ASAPScheduleAnalysis

target = Target(num_qubits=3, dt=1)
target.add_instruction(
    XGate(),
    {(qubit,): InstructionProperties(duration=200) for qubit in range(3)},
)
target.add_instruction(
    Measure(),
    {(qubit,): InstructionProperties(duration=1000) for qubit in range(3)},
)

circuit = QuantumCircuit(3, 1)
circuit.measure(0, 0)
with circuit.if_test((0, True)) as else_:
    circuit.x(1)
with else_:
    circuit.x(2)
with circuit.if_test((0, True)) as else_:
    circuit.x(2)
with else_:
    circuit.x(1)

analysis = PassManager([ASAPScheduleAnalysis(target=target)])
analysis.run(circuit)
expected = [
    start_time
    for node, start_time in analysis.property_set["node_start_time"].items()
    if isinstance(node.op, ControlFlowOp)
]

analysis_and_padding = PassManager(
    [
        ASAPScheduleAnalysis(target=target),
        PadDelay(target=target, schedule_idle_qubits=True),
    ]
)
analysis_and_padding.run(circuit)
actual = [
    start_time
    for node, start_time in analysis_and_padding.property_set["node_start_time"].items()
    if isinstance(node.op, ControlFlowOp)
]

assert actual == expected
```

The final assertion fails because the rebuilt control-flow operations do not retain their scheduled block indices.

**Expected behavior**

Padding should preserve the scheduled `(block_idx, start_time)` metadata for rebuilt control-flow operations. Returning from a nested block visit should restore the parent's timing state, and a final fast-path barrier should receive the parent block index and duration in the documented argument order.

**Suggested solutions**

- Preserve and restore `_idle_after` and `_current_block_idx` around `_visit_block()` recursion.
- Keep the scheduled block index separate from the control-flow body-loop index.
- Pass `prev_block_idx, prev_block_duration` to the final `_add_block_terminating_barrier()` call.
- Add regressions for sequential multi-branch control flow and nested state restoration.

**Additional Information**

- **qiskit-ibm-runtime version**: current `main`; also observed in 0.47.0
- **Python version**: 3.11.8
- **Operating system**: macOS
- Proposed fix: #3076

issue.title: Write tests to verify parameter-basis expansion performed in executor-based Estimator

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Exists, but can be done better, faster, or different

issue.body:
When mapping a `pub = (circuit, observables, parameter_values)` into a quantum program item, the various `prepare_*` functions used in executor-based Estimator undertake the same steps:
- They pre-compute `evs.shape` as `np.broadcast_shapes(observables.shape, parameter_values.shape)`.
- They create a map between elements of `parameter_values` and the observables that need to be measured for each subset.
- They replace the observables in that map with the minimal set of Pauli basis that can be used to measure all such observables.

As an example, consider the case where:
- `observables = ObservablesArray(["ZZZ", "XXX", "YYY", "IYI"]).reshape((2, 2))` has shape `(2, 2)`.
- `parameter_values` has shape `(2, 2)` as well.

In this case, `evs` has shape `(2, 2)`, and such mapping amounts to:
- `((0, 0), "ZZZ")`, meaning that the "first" element in `parameter_values`, indexed with `(0, 0)`, needs to be measured with basis `"ZZZ"`
- `((0, 1), "XXX")`
- `((1, 0), "YYY")`
- `((1, 1), "IYI")`

This mapping is currently stored inside the passthrough data of the quantum program.

### Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Add tests that demonstrate that every `prepare_*` function computes this mapping correctly.
- [ ] Make these tests consistent across every `prepare_*` function

- As well as an asymmetry with `SamplerV2`: in Sampler, we have a single `prepare` function that takes as input pubs and options and returns pubs and options, mapping inputs of Sampler to inputs of Executor.

TODOs:

- [ ] Write a `prepare` function that takes inputs of Estimator and maps them to inputs of Executor, taking care of dispatching to the low-level `prepare_*` functions.
- [ ] Rewrite tests such as `test_run_dispatches_to_prepare_pec_when_pec_enabled` in a way that does not require mocks

issue.title: Estimate primitive QPU usage before submission

labels.name: feature
labels.description: New feature or addition to the project

type.name: Feature request
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
**What is the expected feature?**

It would be useful to estimate the QPU usage of a complete `SamplerV2` or `EstimatorV2` workload before submitting it.

Currently, `RuntimeJobV2.usage_estimation` provides the service estimate only after a job has been submitted, while `max_execution_time` is a cancellation limit rather than a forecast.

IBM documents a local baseline approximation:

```text
per-sub-job overhead + (repetition delay + circuit duration) * number of executions
```

One possible API would be:

```python
sampler_estimate = sampler.estimate_usage(pubs, shots=4096)
estimator_estimate = estimator.estimate_usage(pubs, precision=0.02)
```

The result could report:

- Estimated QPU usage in quantum seconds.
- Circuit execution count.
- Circuit, reset, repetition-delay, and overhead contributions.
- Backend and calibration provenance.
- Assumptions, warnings, confidence, and whether the result is a lower bound.

Individual estimates could also be combined to plan batch or session workloads. Session estimates would necessarily be lower bounds because actual session usage can include classical processing and idle reservation time.

Monetary conversion would remain out of scope because pricing depends on the user's plan and instance.

I have a working client-side prototype/tool that performs this calculation from primitive inputs and backend metadata without submitting a job or creating a session. I would be happy to adapt and contribute it based on maintainer guidance.

Questions for maintainers:

1. Does this functionality belong directly on `SamplerV2` and `EstimatorV2`, or would a standalone utility be preferable?
2. Should the result be a structured estimate with provenance and warnings, or only a numeric duration?
3. Should batch and session aggregation be part of the initial API?
4. Is a client-side approximation acceptable when server-side mitigation and sub-job splitting cannot be predicted exactly?
5. Should input coercion and validation be shared with `run()` to ensure estimation and submission interpret workloads identically?

**Acceptance criteria**

- Estimate Sampler and Estimator workloads without submitting them.
- Respect PUB broadcasting and shot or precision precedence.
- Use backend target durations when available.
- Fall back to the documented quick approximation when detailed durations are unavailable.
- Clearly identify low-confidence and lower-bound estimates.
- Never create a job, batch, or session.
- Return QPU usage seconds.

Related prior work:

- #479 considered client-side estimation for circuit-runner jobs.
- #972 and #976 added the post-submission `usage_estimation` interface.

IBM documentation: https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/en/guides/estimate-job-run-time

We are working on a new estimation service that will provide more accurate estimations through a different mechanism. As this service is envisaged to have quite some overlap with you use case and your prototypes features, as well as having some practical implications in the package's API and functionality, we'd rather not accept estimation-related contributions at this point in time, unfortunately. 

Hopefully the eventual service will cater to your specific needs - and again, thanks for the suggestion and the effort.

issue.title: Facilitate unit testing of QiskitRuntimeService

labels.name: type: QA
labels.description: Issues and PRs that relate to testing and code quality

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Exists, but can be done better, faster, or different

issue.body:
**What is the expected enhancement?**

Currently, `QiskitRuntimeService` contains quite a number of "state" variables, that are populated and modified through complex nested logic. A number of these variables also depend on the instances and account configuration and properties which are difficult to replicate - overall, this limits our ability to effectively test it locally and have good confidence about it. The natural trend is to resort to integration testing, but this is also limited when it comes to testing instance, plans and accounts combinations.

We have `FakeRuntimeService` and the family at `test/unit/mock` as a way to mitigate. These classes provide alternative implementations, but override/mock some of the methods, which causes the real logic not to be exercised (and require these counterparts to be maintained and kept on par). A number of tests depend on specific "tweaks" over the state variables, and have a risk of testing the fake counterparts rather than the actual classes. At some point in time `FakeRuntimeService` and related classes allowed for customization of instances and other features, but part of their functionality seems to be out of date.

This story is about providing testing facilities that allow for testing `QiskitRuntimeService` with more confidence.

**Acceptance criteria**

More unit tests in the codebase use `QiskitRuntimeService` directly.

issue.title: Add wrapper options validations

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Exists, but can be done better, faster, or different

issue.body: There are several option validations that are present in the legacy options that haven't been ported to the wrapper options classes. The goal of this issue is to identify where they differ, and which ones should continue to function in the wrapper options.

issue.title: Wrapper options silently drop numeric validators present in legacy options
issue.body:
Legacy `EstimatorOptions` rejects a handful of clearly-invalid numeric inputs at construction time — `default_precision <= 0`, `default_shots < 0`, `twirling.num_randomizations/shots_per_randomization = 0`, `measure_noise_learning.num_randomizations = 0`, and `pec.max_overhead = 0` (this last one got tightened from `gt=0` to `ge=0`, so negatives are still caught, but 0 now slips through).

None of these validators exist on the executor-wrapper side. A value that used to raise immediately now gets silently accepted and only fails later (or not at all) once it hits run() or the server.

issue.title: Wrapper doesn't validate measure_noise_learning against measure_mitigation at construction
issue.body:
In legacy options, setting `resilience.measure_noise_learning` fields while `measure_mitigation` is `False` trips a `model_validator` and raises right away — you find out immediately that the config doesn't make sense.

On the wrapper side there's no equivalent validator. The value just gets silently forwarded as `None` at `run()` time, so the user gets no signal that their `measure_noise_learning` config was ignored.

issue.title: Wrapper accepts ZNE configs with too few noise_factors for the chosen extrapolator
issue.body:
Legacy raises at construction if you pick an extrapolator that needs more points than you gave it — e.g. `double_exponential` needs at least 4 `noise_factors`, and the legacy `model_validator` catches an under-specified combination immediately.

The wrapper has no such check. The bad config is accepted, and the under-specified fit just fails later — either deeper in client code or server-side — instead of failing fast with a clear message.

Worth adding the same cross-field validation so users get the error where they made the mistake, not several layers downstream.

comments.body:
Continuing but not as a options validator since it causes mutation order side effects. 

For example this is the behavior from the legacy that should not be reproduced:

```
# this works
legacy = LegacyEstimator(mode=backend)
legacy.options.resilience.zne_mitigation = True
legacy.options.resilience.zne.noise_factors = [1, 3, 4, 5]
legacy.options.resilience.zne.extrapolator = "double_exponential" 

# this doesnt
legacy = LegacyEstimator(mode=backend)
legacy.options.resilience.zne_mitigation = True
legacy.options.resilience.zne.extrapolator = "double_exponential" 
legacy.options.resilience.zne.noise_factors = [1, 3, 4, 5]
```

The solution is to put the validation later in the workflow.

issue.title: Wrapper defers the pec/zne mutual-exclusion check from construction to run()
issue.body:
Legacy rejects `pec_mitigation=True` together with `zne_mitigation=True` at construction — you can't even build the invalid options object.

The wrapper still rejects this combination, but only at `run()` time instead of construction. Functionally it still errors, so this is more of a timing regression than a correctness one — but it means the invalid state can exist and get passed around (logged, serialized, inspected) before the check ever fires.

Low urgency compared to the others since it does still error, but flagging since it changes when a user finds out.

comments.body: Adding a options validation causes issues with `finalize_options` since the validation will trip after the finalization. Therefore it is best to just allow `run()` to raise the error.

issue.title: Tests relying on specs order are flaky
issue.body:
### Details
The specs returned by `samplex.inputs().specs` are sorted alphabetically. However, spec index is advanced numerically `1,2,3,...`, and when the number of decimal places in the index changes (`99, 100` for example), the alphabetical order does not match the insertion order. If the test relies on the order of the specs to judge the insertion order, it will be flaky and could fail depending on the exact value of the reference counter. The test will then fail or pass depending on test execution order, OS and other factors making it extremely hard to debug.

For example this test [here](https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/blob/6c7a627186f33b8b418d2bbd12cb61966385b153/test/unit/executor_estimator/test_estimator_v2_prepare_vanilla.py#L224).

issue.title: Enable VPE support for Qiskit Functions by adding `QISKIT_IBM_PRIVATE_ENDPOINT` environment variable

labels.name: feature
labels.description: New feature or addition to the project

type.name: Feature request
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
**What is the expected feature?**

Qiskit Functions run `QiskitRuntimeService` inside a container to submit and manage quantum jobs. We have been able to access the runtime service through the public network, but as we shift towards a VPE-based network model, containers must route all IBM Cloud traffic through **private** endpoints. 

While a `private_endpoint` option exists in the runtime client, `private_endpoint=True` can only be set in code. This is different to all other connection parameters (`QISKIT_IBM_URL`, `QISKIT_IBM_TOKEN`, `QISKIT_IBM_INSTANCE`) which can be injected as environment variables at deploy time. Not having an environment value makes it impossible to enable private endpoints in Qiskit Function containers without modifying the function source code.

**Additional bugs found while investigating private endpoints**

- The private endpoint hostnames generated for Global Search and Global Catalog are incorrect and do not match the actual VPE endpoints, causing `instances()` and CRN validation to fail.
- When a fully-qualified CRN is passed as instance, `QiskitRuntimeService.__init__` still calls `instances()` to validate it, which is redundant and triggers unnecessary catalog and search traffic.

**Acceptance criteria**

Setting `QISKIT_IBM_PRIVATE_ENDPOINT=true` should be equivalent to passing private_endpoint=True, consistent with how other connection parameters work. Combined with `QISKIT_IBM_URL`, this allows a Qiskit Function container to be fully configured for a VPE environment via environment variables injected at deploy time, with no code changes required.

**Note**

I already have a local fix for the 3 points mentioned above, verified with the Qiskit Functions VPE, and will follow up with a PR shortly. I still wanted to open an issue to document the context around these changes.

issue.title: Decide the fate of `selected_extrapolators`

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Exists, but can be done better, faster, or different

issue.body:
**What is the expected enhancement?**
Following the merger of #2953 the ZNE extrapolation pathway computes the `selected_extrapolators`, but it is not reflected in the result handed back to the user. The property is motivated by a similar property that existed in the past in the legacy estimator (but no longer is).

As it stands, the `selected_extrapolators` object contains the choice of extrapolator for every term in every observable in every configuration (=parameter set) for every extrapolated noise level (with 0 added to the values requested by the user). This choice is not very informative, as different extrapolated values are computed differently. Namely:

- `evs` - extrapolation to 0 noise which is done with a mixed strategy. Each term is extrapolated on its own, the best extrapolator is chosen, and then summed to get observable expectation value. This means that more than one extrapolation method could be used in the estimation of a single observable. This is where the selection process is relevant.
- `evs_extrapolated` - extrapolation to the user specified noise levels. Here the returned values are not using the same mixed extrapolation strategy but rather include the expectation value for each extrapolation method, where terms are using the same strategy (i.e. one result where all terms use linear extrapolation, one result where all terms use exponential extrapolation and so on, and no mixed extrapolation). In this case no selection needs to be made (though it is).

So, the `selected_extrapolators` are only relevant when the mixed extrapolation strategy is used, but that in turn only happens with the mandatory extrapolation to 0 noise. The selection for other extrapolated noise levels doesn't have any effect on the results the user gets back (and does not help with calculating the results, because the user doesn't get back the results per term).

**Acceptance criteria**
We need to:

1. Decide what, if any, do we want to return to the user when it comes to `selected_extrapolators`?
2. Compute only the needed values, and return them to the user.

comments.body: #3166 will resolve many of the problems we've encountered. Furthermore, contrary to what the issue says the selected extrapolators are reported in the legacy pathway (in a way consistent with #3166) as part of the pub metadata.

issue.title: Improve documentation of ZNE results

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Exists, but can be done better, faster, or different

issue.body:
**What is the expected enhancement?**
ZNE returns many fields in its data bin:

- 'evs'
- 'stds'
- 'evs_noise_factors'
- 'stds_noise_factors'
- 'ensemble_stds_noise_factors'
- 'evs_extrapolated'
- 'stds_extrapolated'

Some values are similar to those available with other error mitigation techniques, others are unique to ZNE and each one is computed differently (sometimes in a non-trivial way) - even their shapes are sometimes non-trivial. We need to better document what each field represents and how it is calculated. As those values are being calculated by a series of functions using similar variable names we also need to decide *where* this should documented - is it every function doing some of the computation? Only the client facing ones? Only external guides?

Another thing which needs better documentation are conventions - what happens when extrapolation fails? What do we get back then? Currently, the user get back an inf.

**Acceptance criteria**
The extent of the needed documentation is discussed and applied.

issue.title: Populate metadata in `run_quantum_program` results

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Exists, but can be done better, faster, or different

issue.body:
**What is the expected enhancement?**

There are two types of metadata:
- Global - attached to the execution result
- Local - per input pub

No metadata is populated currently.

Internally we run Aer's `SamplerV2`, which returns both global and local metadata:
- The global metadata contains a single key: `version`
- The local metadata keys are `shots`, `circuit_metadata`, `simulator_metadata`

For the executor, I suggest to:
- Ignore the version for now, and return empty global metadata
- Return the same local metadata as the sampler

Note two problems with my suggestion:
- The real executor returns empty local metadata (possibly to be removed), since it uses the pass through data for returning this type of information
- The local metadata doesn't match the executor schema

However also for the other simulators, for example the sampler simulator, the metadata doesn't match the schema, and what's returned from the real device. It makes sense to me, because the schemas' context is the contract with the server via Rest API, which is irrelevant for the simulators.


**Acceptance criteria**

For the executor simulator, return the same local metadata as the sampler.

comments.body: We should coordinate on this one, because as part of #3046 we are considering changes to some metadata conventions. Namely, some fields which were previously pub-level are no longer set at the pub level, and could potentially move to the program level.

Part of the discussion should be how much the simulators should align with results returned from real devices. My opinion is that it's ok to diverge: devices return a lot of information about chunking, scheduling, and stretches, while simulators return information about time taken, memory consumption, and parallelization. But I agree that we should take a closer look at what's done as part of #3406, and decide individually for each change whether to apply it also for the simulator.

issue.title: FakeProviderForBackendV2 missing 8 newer fake backends (FakeAachen, FakeBerlin, FakeBoston, FakeBrussels, FakeKingston, FakeMiami, FakePittsburgh, FakeStrasbourg)

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

issue.body:
## Environment
qiskit-ibm-runtime: 0.48.0 (latest on PyPI)

## What happened
`FakeProviderForBackendV2` is documented as containing "all fake V2 backends available in the `qiskit_ibm_runtime.fake_provider`" module, and its docs page states it uses the list from the module's own backend page.

However, name-based lookup fails for the following backends that clearly exist and are directly importable:
- `FakeAachen`, 
- `FakeBerlin`, 
- `FakeBoston`, 
- `FakeBrussels`, 
- `FakeKingston`,
- `FakeMiami`,
- `FakePittsburgh`, and
- `FakeStrasbourg`

```python
from qiskit_ibm_runtime.fake_provider import FakeKingston
FakeKingston().num_qubits  # 156, works fine

from qiskit_ibm_runtime.fake_provider import FakeProviderForBackendV2
FakeProviderForBackendV2().backend(name="fake_kingston")
# QiskitBackendNotFoundError
```

Looking at [`FakeProviderForBackendV2.__init__`](https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/blob/stable/0.48/qiskit_ibm_runtime/fake_provider/fake_provider.py#L29-L116), `self._backends` is a hardcoded list literal that simply never includes `FakeKingston` (or 7 others). There's no conditional logic, feature flag, or comment explaining the omission.

## Reproduction: full list of missing classes

```python
from qiskit_ibm_runtime.fake_provider import FakeProviderForBackendV2
import qiskit_ibm_runtime.fake_provider as fp

provider = FakeProviderForBackendV2()
registered = {type(b).__name__ for b in provider.backends()}
all_classes = {n for n in dir(fp) if n.startswith("Fake") and n != "FakeProviderForBackendV2"}
print(sorted(all_classes - registered))
```
```
['FakeAachen', 'FakeBerlin', 'FakeBoston', 'FakeBrussels', 'FakeKingston',
 'FakeMiami', 'FakePittsburgh', 'FakeStrasbourg']
```

## Expected behavior
`FakeProviderForBackendV2().backend(name="fake_kingston")` (and the other 7) should resolve, matching the class's own documentation and matching user expectations given the classes exist and are directly importable.

## Suggested fix
Add the 8 missing classes to the hardcoded list, ideally via a more maintainable mechanism (e.g. auto-discovering `Fake*` subclasses of `FakeBackendV2` in the module) so this doesn't silently recur as new devices are added in future releases.

### Details

issue.title: `PauliLindbladMap` noise models fail to serialize in executor-wrapper `EstimatorV2` submission (PEA/PEC)

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

issue.body:
## Summary
Submitting a real, non-identity `resilience.noise_model_mapping` through the executor-backed `EstimatorV2` (`qiskit_ibm_runtime.executor_estimator.estimator.EstimatorV2`) fails at job submission with a wall of ~60 `pydantic.ValidationError`s. The errors come from trying to fit `PauliLindbladMap.GeneratorTerm` objects into a passthrough schema that only accepts numeric/bool/string leaves.

## Where it happens
Not a legacy-`EstimatorV2` issue — only the executor-wrapper path. Reproduced with PEA (`amplifier="pea"`); PEC goes through the identical code path and is expected to fail identically.

## Root cause
`executor_estimator/estimator.py` echoes finalized options into `passthrough_data` for server-side reporting. 

```python
quantum_program.passthrough_data["post_processor"]["options"] = options.model_dump()
```

## Impact
Any real PEA or PEC run using a `NoiseLearnerV3`-learned noise model fails on submission — after the noise-learning job (and its QPU time) has already been spent. High blast radius for anyone exercising real PEC/PEA workflows on the executor path.

## Repro
Synthetic non-identity `PauliLindbladMap.from_list([("XX", 0.001), ("ZZ", 0.002)])` against a mock backend, per the reproducer notebook.

comments.body: Resolved via #3268

issue.title: Executor_sampler/executor_estimator cannot execute non-Clifford rzz gates

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
[`box_builder.py:129`](https://github.com/Qiskit/samplomatic/blob/487202826012c15385149fe80e83f3b9cbb97166/samplomatic/builders/box_builder.py#L129) in `samplomatic` raises `BuildError` for any non-Clifford or unbound fractional
entangler (`rzz`) unless the pass manager's twirling group is `local_pauli`. But both Executor
primitives choose the group internally and never pass `local_pauli`:

- `executor_sampler/prepare.py:142` calls `generate_boxing_pass_manager()` with no `twirling_group` arg.
- in `executor_estimator/utils.py` `options_to_boxing_pm_kwargs(..., twirling_group: str =
  "balanced_pauli", ...)`. but the [call sites](https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/blob/718fb5292eae222c327bf4627e38c31ae1b8f65c/qiskit_ibm_runtime/executor_estimator/utils.py#L323) and [`prepare_vanilla.py`](https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/blob/718fb5292eae222c327bf4627e38c31ae1b8f65c/qiskit_ibm_runtime/executor_estimator/prepare_vanilla.py#L102) do not override it.


**Steps to reproduce**

```python
from qiskit.circuit import QuantumCircuit, Parameter
from qiskit.transpiler.preset_passmanagers import generate_preset_pass_manager
from qiskit_ibm_runtime.fake_provider import FakeFractionalBackend
from qiskit_ibm_runtime.executor_sampler import SamplerV2

backend = FakeFractionalBackend()
theta = Parameter("theta")
qc = QuantumCircuit(2, 2)
qc.h(0)
qc.rzz(theta, 0, 1)            # non-Clifford, unbound fractional entangler
qc.h(0)
qc.measure([0, 1], [0, 1])
isa = generate_preset_pass_manager(optimization_level=1, backend=backend).run(qc)

sampler = SamplerV2(mode=backend)
sampler.options.twirling.enable_gates = True
sampler.options.experimental = {"local_mode": True}
sampler.run([(isa, {"theta": 0.9})], shots=256).result()
```

**Expected behavior**

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
...
...
samplomatic.exceptions.BuildError: Non-Clifford and unbound fractional entanglers are only
supported for Twirl with 'GroupMode LOCAL_PAULI'.
```
`EstimatorV2` on the equivalent observable pub raises the identical `BuildError` from the same line.

**Suggested solutions**

**1. Example minimal fix: look at the circuit first, then decide.** Before boxing, scan the pubs for
an `rzz` that's still a free parameter or bound to anything other than a quarter-turn (π/2), the one
case that actually needs the special 8-Pauli group. If found, switch to it for that call; if not,
leave everything exactly as it is.
(or)
We may add/retain the explicit `twirling_group` field to `TwirlingOptions` that a user sets themselves, however the auto-detect version is the less invasive of the two for the identical outcome: the field-based version needs a new pydantic field.

Example diff of the first, less invasive approach:

```diff
--- a/qiskit_ibm_runtime/executor_estimator/utils.py
+++ b/qiskit_ibm_runtime/executor_estimator/utils.py
@@
+from samplomatic.constants import SUPPORTED_2Q_FRACTIONAL_GATES
+
+def _needs_local_pauli(pubs: Iterable[EstimatorPub]) -> bool:
+    """Whether any pub contains a fractional gate that only "local_pauli" can twirl."""
+    return any(
+        instr.operation.name in SUPPORTED_2Q_FRACTIONAL_GATES
+        and (
+            instr.operation.is_parameterized()
+            or not np.allclose(np.abs(instr.operation.params), np.pi / 2)
+        )
+        for pub in pubs
+        for instr in pub.circuit.data
+    )
+
 def options_to_boxing_pm_kwargs(
     twirling_options, measure_noise_learning, inject_noise,
     twirling_group: str = "balanced_pauli", add_tags: bool = False,
+    pubs: Iterable[EstimatorPub] | None = None,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    if pubs is not None and _needs_local_pauli(pubs):
+        twirling_group = "local_pauli"
     return {...}
```
A longer effort may have a clearer division of burdens, or have a clear optional pathway for the same, and shall not involve the recounting of `rzz` gates on the `qiskit-ibm-runtime` end, rather, to recycle the template and pubs as created by the `passmanager` in `Samplomatic` as-is. This will leave only the execution pipeline here, without squashing the template into a new one via the default executor path.

comments.body: Thanks for opening this, @aaryav3. As discussed today, we will likely go with something along the lines of the second option, as the first option ("look at the circuit, then decide") is expensive, as it requires a loop.

issue.title: Wrapper estimator underestimates reported uncertainties with multi-term observables

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
In the post processor we sum the contributions to the variance term by term
```python
ensemble_variance += (coeff**2) * term_ensemble_variance * (term_scale_factor**2)
twirl_variance   += (coeff**2) * term_twirl_variance    * (term_scale_factor**2)
```
However, this is only justified when each term is an independent variable. This is not the case with commuting terms - these are based on the same shots. Therefore, the covariance contributions are not accounted for. To correctly estimate the uncertainty we need to group terms by their `config_idx` and compute the variance for the group together.

The bug applies to multi-term observables with commuting terms - for example `Z + ZZ`. Currently the simulation tests decompose projectors into paulis, automatically creating such commuting terms (related to #3225 and #3243).

issue.body:
**What is the expected enhancement?**

In the legacy primitives, the `TwirlingOptions` [docstrings](https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/blob/91df674e01fdf98fbfcb326b47e85b96c6fe2893/qiskit_ibm_runtime/options/twirling_options.py#L52-L90) tells me the how the `num_randomizations` and `shots_per_randomization` are calculated. 

For example, if I specify `default_shots=1024` and use default values for twirling options, I can expect 
- shots_per_randomization = max(64, ceil(shots / 32)) = 64 and
- num_randomizations = ceil(shots/shots_per_randomization) = 16

In the wrapper primitive, however, the [docstrings](https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/blob/91df674e01fdf98fbfcb326b47e85b96c6fe2893/qiskit_ibm_runtime/options_models/twirling.py#L60-L70) just say "the value is determined automatically based on the input PUB and other options". There is no (easy) information on the number of randomizations or total shots. 

Even if I turn on logging, I see 

> TREX calibration circuit added (16 randomizations).
> Submitting 2 pubs to executor with 2112 total shots

But no information on where that 2112 comes from and how it relates to `default_shots=1024`

**Acceptance criteria**

I should be able to find out the number of randomization, shots per randomization, and total number of shots from job metadata.

issue.title: Make mypy configuration more strict and aware of third-party dependencies

labels.name: type: QA
labels.description: Issues and PRs that relate to testing and code quality

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Exists, but can be done better, faster, or different

issue.body:
**What is the expected enhancement?**

Currently, the `mypy` configuration is quite lax. In particular, it does not take third-party dependencies into account, which places some limits on the amount of type infering that can be enforced, as well as having the potential for tine tuning further. This causes some typing issues only available when using other checkers (ie. IDEs using pyright) that can hide potential bugs.

This story is not about achieving 100% precise typing of the library, but about reaching a state where we can enable third-party dependency checking and a better balance when it comes to opaquing typing issues (ideally being caught by the automated `mypy` run). There are some relatively complex items to tackle:
* our usage of `| None`  in multiple places with `None` as a placeholder that is populated and whether coercion can take place
* constraints from third-party libraries that might not be declaring type hints fully
* imprecise or historical typing (`Backend` vs `BackendV2`; the `mode` handling)

The plan is to tackle this issue incrementally, and reevaluate the balance progress is made.

Some relation to #2514 (some ignores are likely to be made unneeded as more items are properly fixed - and some new ones are likely to be needed for typing issues from upstream).

**Acceptance criteria**

Our `mypy` configuration takes into account third-party dependencies, and the configuration is able to detect more legitimate issues.

issue.title: `xslow` (via `XSlowGate`) can't be exported to QASM3 and is lost when exported as QPY

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

- Using the qasm3 exporter fails if the circuit contains a `XSlowGate`.
- QPY doesn't preserve the `XSlowGate` subclass. A circuit saved with `XSlowGate` comes back with a plain `Gate` named "xslow" after `qpy.load`.

**Steps to reproduce**

```python
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit, qasm3
from qiskit_ibm_runtime.circuit.library import XSlowGate 

qc = QuantumCircuit(1, 1)
qc.append(XSlowGate(), [0])
qc.measure(0, 0)

qasm3.dumps(qc)
```

Fails with:

```
qiskit.qasm3.exceptions.QASM3ExporterError: "failed to export gate 'xslow' that has no definition"
```

Also this shows the XSlowGate class is lost at QPY serialization:

```python
import io
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit, qasm3, qpy
from qiskit_ibm_runtime.circuit.library import XSlowGate

qc = QuantumCircuit(1, 1)
qc.append(XSlowGate(), [0])
qc.measure(0, 0)

buf = io.BytesIO()
qpy.dump(qc, buf)
buf.seek(0)
qc2 = qpy.load(buf)[0]

op = qc2.data[0].operation
print(type(op).__name__, op.definition)  # -> Gate None
```


**Expected behavior**

QASM3 export works.

**Suggested solutions**
- Add a placeholder body in `XSlowGate.__init__`:

```python
class XSlowGate(Gate):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__("xslow", 1, [])
        self.definition = QuantumCircuit(1)   # empty placeholder body
```

- I believe QPY has no registration mechanism for third-party Gate subclasses; so maybe just documentation/caveat note in XSlowGate's docstring

**Additional Information**

- **qiskit-ibm-runtime version**:
- **Python version**:
- **Operating system**:

comments.body:
We experience similar issues when replacing xslow in the examples above with `qc.append(MidCircuitMeasure(), [0], [0])`.

In the first case (qasm3 exporter) we obtain an error, but it's not about the instruction definition this time:
```
qiskit.qasm3.exceptions.QASM3ExporterError: "non-unitary subroutine calls are not yet supported, but received 'Instruction(name='measure_2', num_qubits=1, num_clbits=1, params=[])'"
```

The second case (class preservation) is more similar:
```
Instruction None
```

About class preservation, note that the instruction name is preserved. This is important, because this is what makes everything work, although the server loads qpy payload that the client dumped. The server sees a generic `Gate` whose name is `xslow`, and this is enough for the xslow gate to be executed, there is no need for the class to be `XSlowGate`, as along as the gate name is `xslow`.

About the qasm3 exporter, the solution of a dummy definition to make the exporter happy can be problematic, because the definition is used in transpilation. For example this code runs, where I'd want it to fail (it fails if we omit the line that sets a definition):
```python
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit, transpile
from qiskit_ibm_runtime import QiskitRuntimeService
from qiskit_ibm_runtime.circuit.library import XSlowGate


backend = QiskitRuntimeService().backend("ibm_boston")

xslow = XSlowGate()
xslow.definition = QuantumCircuit(1)

qc = QuantumCircuit(1, 1)
qc.append(xslow, [0])
qc.measure(0, 0)

transpile(qc, basis_gates=["cz", "id", "rz", "sx", "x"])
```

I checked a bit the options of registering a gate to qasm3, and it doesn't look promising. We can instruct our users to set the `basis_gates` argument of `dump` and `dumps`, but we seek for a solution that will not require anything from the users. We can monkey-patch `dumps`, but it will be ugly.

@jakelishman Can you please try to propose something? TL;DR it appears that `definition` has two different usages: one for the transpiler and another one for the qasm3 exporter. We want the definition to be `None` for the transpiler to work properly, but then it makes the qasm3 exporter fail.
@jakelishman Can you please check also the second sub-issue, the one with qpy?

> We can instruct our users to set the `basis_gates` argument of [`qasm3`'s] `dump` and `dumps`

This is the correct solution.  `xslow` is not a gate in OQ3, so Qiskit can't decide to export a symbol with no definition without user input.  The override for that is `basis_gates`, which means "treat this symbol as externally defined".  Note also that Qiskit (and any other general-purpose OQ3 parser) will refuse to load an OQ3 file like this because it's invalid without a definition - you have to be using a special parser that knows to expect `xslow` as defined elsewhere.

Other gates, like `x`, typically work because they're in the default `stdgates.inc` include file, and Qiskit emits an include statement for that by default.

> QPY doesn't preserve the `XSlowGate` subclass.

This is the defined behaviour of QPY.  We explicitly _don't_ allow the QPY file itself to specify classes/constructors for objects that are not owned by Qiskit SDK itself, for security reasons.

Are you encountering any issues because the subclass is not retained?  In general, it should be sufficient to examine the gate name.  If you are, we can potentially discuss feature additions.

issue.body: **Describe the bug** Suppose you submit two distinct dynamic circuits into a job and request the timeline drawings with `"experimental": {"execution": {"scheduler_timing": True, "stretch_values": True}}`. The outputted scheduler_timing can sometimes not match the expected circuit (i.e., the mapping of circuit <--> scheduler_timing is stochastic and can be wrong). This is probably easier to understand by a couple of pictures... In this job, the timeline drawing matches the circuit expected, but it clashes in this job that I submitted soon after: **Steps to reproduce** Run the following with an existing IBM Quantum saved account: ```sh python -m pip install qiskit==2.5.2 qiskit-ibm-runtime==0.48.0 python minimal.py YOUR_SAVED_ACCOUNT_NAME ``` The script submits six consecutive jobs with identical circuits in order `[2, 0, 1]`, 128 shots per circuit. `circuit_id` is a label stored in circuit metadata. ```python """python minimal.py [saved-account-name]; submits six consecutive jobs.""" import csv import io QiskitRuntimeService, RuntimeEncoder, SamplerV2 def make_circuit(circuit_id): qc = QuantumCircuit(2, 2) qc.metadata = {"circuit_id": circuit_id} for step in range(circuit_id + 1): qc.h(0) qc.barrier() qc.measure(0, 0) if circuit_id: s = qc.add_stretch(f"c{circuit_id}_r{step}") qc.delay(s, 1) qc.x(1) qc.delay(s, 1) qc.delay(s, 1) qc.x(1) qc.delay(s, 1) with qc.if_test((qc.clbits[0], 1)): qc.x(1) qc.barrier() qc.measure(1, 1) return qc def show(job_id, result): print(f"job_id={job_id}", flush=True) for pub in result: circuit_id = pub.metadata["circuit_metadata"]["circuit_id"] timing = pub.metadata["compilation"]["scheduler_timing"]["timing"] qubits = sorted({int(row[2].split()[1]) for row in csv.reader(io.StringIO(timing)) if row[5] == "play" and row[2].startswith("Qubit ")}) expected = [2 * circuit_id, 2 * circuit_id + 1] print(f" circuit_id={circuit_id}: expected={expected}, " f"scheduler_timing={qubits}, match={qubits == expected}", flush=True) def main(): service = QiskitRuntimeService(name=sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None) backend = service.backend("ibm_marrakesh", use_fractional_gates=False) circuits = [generate_preset_pass_manager( backend=backend, optimization_level=0, seed_transpiler=12345, initial_layout=[2 * i, 2 * i + 1], ).run(make_circuit(i)) for i in [2, 0, 1]] sampler = SamplerV2(mode=backend, options={ "dynamical_decoupling": {"enable": False}, "twirling": {"enable_gates": False, "enable_measure": False}, "experimental": {"execution": {"scheduler_timing": True, "stretch_values": True}}, }) # New directory prevents accidentally overwriting a previous run. out = Path("consecutive_jobs") out.mkdir(exist_ok=False) with (out / "circuits.qpy").open("wb") as f: qpy.dump(circuits, f) for run in range(6): job = sampler.run(circuits, shots=128) # Identical circuits and order each time. (out / f"job{run}.txt").write_text(job.job_id()) print(f"submitted run={run} job_id={job.job_id()}", flush=True) result = job.result() (out / f"result{run}.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, cls=RuntimeEncoder)) inputs = job.inputs["pubs"] assert all(p[0] == c for p, c in zip(inputs, circuits, strict=True)) assert [p.metadata["circuit_metadata"] for p in result] == [c.metadata for c in circuits] show(job.job_id(), result) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` Output from the last three consecutive jobs (September 10, 2026): ```text job_id=dahke11hvn6c73cs4i30 circuit_id=2: expected=[4, 5], scheduler_timing=[4, 5], match=True circuit_id=0: expected=[0, 1], scheduler_timing=[0, 1], match=True circuit_id=1: expected=[2, 3], scheduler_timing=[2, 3], match=True job_id=dahke3ni3e6s738nv5p0 circuit_id=2: expected=[4, 5], scheduler_timing=[0, 1], match=False circuit_id=0: expected=[0, 1], scheduler_timing=[4, 5], match=False circuit_id=1: expected=[2, 3], scheduler_timing=[2, 3], match=True job_id=dahke5ni3e6s738nv5rg circuit_id=2: expected=[4, 5], scheduler_timing=[4, 5], match=True circuit_id=0: expected=[0, 1], scheduler_timing=[0, 1], match=True circuit_id=1: expected=[2, 3], scheduler_timing=[2, 3], match=True ``` The middle job exchanges the timelines for circuit IDs 2 and 0. issue.title: `InsertNoisePass` always inserts before/after a barrier

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
The current implementation of `InsertNoisePass` will always inject noise after the tagged barrier unless `noise_after` is set to `False` (note: this option is not exposed to the user). This causes issues e.g. for simulating readout errors as the noise is inserted only after the measurements barrier meaning nothing is applied. 

**Steps to reproduce**
MWE:
```
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.quantum_info import PauliLindbladMap, SparsePauliOp
from qiskit.transpiler.preset_passmanagers import generate_preset_pass_manager
from qiskit_aer import AerSimulator

from qiskit_ibm_runtime.executor_estimator import EstimatorV2

backend = AerSimulator()
circuit = QuantumCircuit(backend.num_qubits)
circuit.measure_all()

preset_pass_manager = generate_preset_pass_manager(backend=backend)

isa_circuit = preset_pass_manager.run(circuit)

observable = SparsePauliOp("Z" * backend.num_qubits)
pub = (isa_circuit, observable)

estimator = EstimatorV2(mode=backend, options={"resilience_level": 0})
estimator.options.simulator.layer_noise_model = [
    (layer, PauliLindbladMap.from_list([("X" * layer.operation.num_qubits, 0.005)])) 
    for layer in estimator.find_unique_layers([pub], types="all")
]

job = estimator.run([pub])
job.result()
print(job.result()[0].data.evs)
```
when `noise_after=True` (default) the expectation value is 1 but when `noise_after=False` it behaves as expected and returns a value <1.

**Expected behavior**
Noise injection via the `InsertNoisePass` should correctly insert noise before or after the barrier depending on the operation e.g. after the ideal gate operation or before the ideal measurement operation.

**Suggested solutions**
One possible solution is to modify the `InsertNoisePass` to work by explicitly identifying barriers but this may require adding and additional `noise_site` argument. 

**Additional Information**

- **qiskit-ibm-runtime version**:
- **Python version**:
- **Operating system**:

comments.body:
I've just been looking into this as well and it seems like we're coming to the same conclusion: 
- An additional `noise_site` field in the `SimulatorOptions` with values `"L"`, `"M"`, `"R"`, `"before"`, `"after"`
- This allows exact specification of the barrier, and `"before"`/`"after"` are convenience options where the specific barrier is chosen based on the context of the box. Before/after here explicitly means a user wants the error to be applied immediately before or after the ideal gate operation in the simulation.

For the before/after auto-choosing, Claude gave me this rule based on how the box is dressed:
```
_SITE_TO_POSITION = {
    (InjectionSite.BEFORE, DressingMode.LEFT): "M",
    (InjectionSite.AFTER, DressingMode.LEFT): "R",
    (InjectionSite.BEFORE, DressingMode.RIGHT): "L",
    (InjectionSite.AFTER, DressingMode.RIGHT): "M",
}
```
It should be verified but I think this is roughly correct.

This string could be added as a third entry in the tuple of `layer_noise_model`, though it will need to be decided what to do with in the `estimator_options_to_executor_options` conversion function.

There are a couple of further issues here:
- Should this specification be kept optional with a default?
- Special case 1: prep noise
   - There is not always a box associated with preparation, and in this case there is no way to assign a model to it. One option is to add another option to `SimulatorOptions` to specify a noise map that happens *before anything else in the circuit*. It is absolutely critical that it happens before anything else happens, so that it is truly appearing immediately after the preparation operation.
   - If there *is* a box associated with it, the body is empty, and I believe it is constrained to be a left-dressed. This is problematic for the above `_SITE_TO_POSITION` choices: in this case the actual operation we want to model occurs before the box, and if we use the above rules the noise map will be inserted AFTER the dressing, which is not what we want. Here, what we really want, is to assign the noise map to the `"L"` barrier.
- Special case 2: a box with only single qubit gates
   - This is again problematic, e.g. if the box is left dressed, having the noise occur after the dressing but `"before"` the layer is impossible, as the single qubit gates get absorbed into the dressing.

For the special cases: we definitely need an option for inserting a noise map at the very beginning of the circuit regardless. For the empty-box case in the prep-noise situation, what we really want is to assign it to the `"L"` barrier, so this could be handled by raising an error if the user specifies `"before"`/`"after"` in this scenario, and tell them to assign it to an explicit barrier. For the single-qubit only case I'm not sure what to do.

issue.title: Add support for simulating estimator jobs with measure mitigation

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Exists, but can be done better, faster, or different

issue.body:
**What is the expected enhancement?**
Currently, simulating estimator jobs with measure mitigation is not supported. In particular, while the simulation inject the measurement noise, a warning warns users that measure mitigation will not be applied to the results.

With qiskit-mitigation PR [#30](https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-mitigation/pull/30), we can remove the warning and ensure that measure mitigation be applied to the results.

**Acceptance criteria**
The following snippet should return `1`:
```python
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.quantum_info import PauliLindbladMap, SparsePauliOp
from qiskit.transpiler.preset_passmanagers import generate_preset_pass_manager
from qiskit_aer import AerSimulator

from qiskit_ibm_runtime.executor_estimator import EstimatorV2

circuit = QuantumCircuit(2)
circuit.h(0)
circuit.cx(0, 1)
circuit.measure_all()

preset_pass_manager = generate_preset_pass_manager(backend:=AerSimulator())

isa_circuit = preset_pass_manager.run(circuit)

observable = SparsePauliOp("X" * circuit.num_qubits)
pub = (isa_circuit, observable)

estimator = EstimatorV2(mode=backend)
estimator.options.twirling.enable_measure = True
estimator.options.resilience.measure_mitigation = True

layers = estimator.find_unique_layers([pub], types="all")
estimator.options.simulator.layer_noise_model = [
    (layer, measure_noise_model) for layer in layers
]

mitigated_result = estimator.run([pub]).result()
mitigated_evs = mitigated_result[0].data.evs
```

issue.title: [P10] Cap the Qiskit major version in the qiskit requirement
issue.body:
Hi! `qiskit-ibm-runtime` is a [Qiskit Ecosystem](https://qiskit.github.io/ecosystem/) member, and one of the weekly [check ups](https://qiskit.github.io/ecosystem/checkups/) is currently failing for it:

> [`[P10]` Have a cap on the major version for the qiskit dependency](https://qiskit.github.io/ecosystem/checkups/#P10)
>
> Python package qiskit-ibm-runtime declared itself compatible to a not-yet-released major version of Qiskit

The qiskit requirement (`qiskit>=2.3.0`) has no upper bound. Qiskit follows semantic versioning, so nothing guarantees the package still works after the next major release, and pip is free to resolve to it the day it lands. Qiskit 3 is not planned yet, but the compatibility claim is already there.

Suggested fix, in `pyproject.toml`:

```diff
     "pydantic>=2.13.0",
-    "qiskit>=2.3.0",
+    "qiskit>=2.3.0,<3",
     "pybase64>=1.4.0",
```

That keeps every Qiskit version you support today; bump the cap once you have tested against the next major release. The check up reads the metadata of the package published on PyPI, so it clears on its own after a release that carries the cap.

Thanks for being part of the ecosystem!

issue.title: Import fails on Windows 11 because unsigned sspilib module is blocked by Smart App Control

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

issue.body: ### Description Importing QiskitRuntimeService fails on Windows 11: from qiskit_ibm_runtime import QiskitRuntimeService The import chain is: qiskit_ibm_runtime → requests_ntlm → spnego → sspilib → sspilib.raw._ntstatus Windows Code Integrity blocks the native module: sspilib\raw\_ntstatus.pyd ### Error ImportError: DLL load failed while importing _ntstatus: An application control policy has blocked this file. Windows Code Integrity events 3077 and 3033 report: "_ntstatus.pyd did not meet the Enterprise signing level requirements or violated code integrity policy." The `_ntstatus.pyd` file distributed through PyPI does not have an Authenticode digital signature. ### Environment - Windows 11 - Python 3.14, 64-bit - qiskit-ibm-runtime installed from PyPI - Smart App Control / Code Integrity enabled - No NTLM proxy is being used ### Possible solutions Would it be possible to: 1. avoid importing `requests_ntlm` and `sspilib` when no NTLM proxy is configured; 2. make NTLM support an optional dependency loaded only when required; or 3. coordinate with the sspilib maintainer to distribute Authenticode-signed Windows `.pyd` files? The sspilib repository currently restricts the creation of new issues, so I could not report the unsigned binary directly upstream. Since @jborean93 maintains sspilib and pyspnego, I am mentioning him here in case he can clarify whether Authenticode-signed Windows wheels could be provided for sspilib.

comments.body:
> Since [Jordan Borean (@jborean93)](https://github.com/jborean93) maintains sspilib and pyspnego, I am mentioning him here
in case he can clarify whether Authenticode-signed Windows wheels could be
provided for sspilib.

It's not something I would do personally to include in the main PyPI package but technically you could you could vendor or bundle your own copy of `sspilib` and sign the `.pyd` files yourself as part of any distribution you do.

In saying that if you are running on a host that has enabled WDAC/App Control or AppLocker you probably don't want to have Python loaded at all. It needs you to allow `python.exe` and it's runtime dlls to run  and trusted but this means you now have a way to execute arbitrary code and bypass the restrictions of WDAC and co. Python just isn't compatible in this world as it hasn't taken the steps like PowerShell to become an [enlightened applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/app-control-for-business/design/script-enforcement#script-enforcement-overview) so itself can validate what Python code it can execute safely.

Hi Jordan,  
Thanks for your explanation. After investigating further, you were right about this.  
It turned out that Windows Smart App Control was enabled on my machine. I initially encountered the issue with sspilib, but later I got exactly the same kind of error when Qiskit tried to import scipy.linalg: Windows blocked SciPy's _flapack native module because of the application control policy.
This made it clear that the issue was not specific to sspilib, but more generally related to running Python and its native dependencies under such a restrictive application-control policy.
After disabling Smart App Control, both sspilib and scipy.linalg worked normally, without any changes to the packages.
So I agree that signing the sspilib .pyd files in the main PyPI package would not really solve the broader problem. A Python application may depend on many other native .pyd and .dll files from NumPy, SciPy, PySide, etc., and those can be subject to the same restrictions.
Thanks again for pointing me in the right direction and for the explanation about Python not being an enlightened application for App Control.
Thanks both for the open conversation and the prompt exchange (and the outcome!). It will help other users that might have encountered this scenario, and provides insightful context.

```python
[circuit.cx](http://circuit.cx/)(0, 1)
circuit.measure_all()
observable = SparsePauliOp("ZZ")

pm = generate_preset_pass_manager(backend=backend, optimization_level=1)
isa_circuit = pm.run(circuit)

main_job = executor.run(main_qp)
```

Maybe use `getattr(program, "_semantic_role", None)` ?

comments.body:
This is related to #3206 and follow-ups - and arguably partly by design.

During these, we settled on "we consider that we use `qiskit_ibm_runtime.QuantumProgram` in all places", and all methods are typed accordingly and make that assumption (ie. the instances [will always have](https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/blob/0.50.0/qiskit_ibm_runtime/quantum_program/quantum_program.py#L81) `_semantic_role`). 

I do agree it would be desirable to be able to run `samplomatic.QuantumProgram` - we could:
* add the ability of building `qiskit_ibm_runtime.QuantumProgram` from a `samplomatic.QuantumProgram`
* with that, either consider it is the user's responsibility to convert, or refine the requirement (which can actually be "executor.run() should accept both inputs")

Keeping the rationale of assuming that we use `qiskit_ibm_runtime.QuantumProgram` allows the package to be consistent and prevents edge cases: so I'm aiming to containing the conversion either to user-land or to very specific and targeted user-facing entry points.

> During these, we settled on "we consider that we use `qiskit_ibm_runtime.QuantumProgram` in all places"

The 0.50.0 release notes had 

> The following entities related to `QuantumProgram` have been moved to the `samplomatic` package ...
> They should now be imported from the `samplomatic.quantum_program` module.

Does this _not_ include `QuantumProgram` itself? Because I for one assumed "related to QP" implied QP as well 😅

> Does this _not_ include `QuantumProgram` itself? Because I for one assumed "related to QP" implied QP as well 😅

It does include it (ie. the original class was moved), but we keep a subclass of `QuantumProgram` as it contains the semantic role, which is key to this package (and that is the one this package considers "the one"). This was mentioned in the release notes too:

> The following QuantumProgram related entities have been moved to the samplomatic package, and qiskit_ibm_runtime uses them as base classes, providing custom classes for the three of them:
> * qiskit_ibm_runtime.quantum_program.QuantumProgram
> * qiskit_ibm_runtime.results.QuantumProgramResult
> * qiskit_ibm_runtime.results.QuantumProgramItemResult

So it might be an issue of release notes clarity/ordering (the section you quoted explicitly not lists `QuantumProgram` precisely for attempting to convey the subtleties).

Requirements-wise, I believe we are good "`executor.run()` should be able to run a `QuantumProgram` generated by `qiskit-mitigation` (or manually constructed), in addition to being able to run a `QuantumProgram` from `qiskit-ibm-runtime`"?

> Requirements-wise, I believe we are good "`executor.run()` should be able to run a `QuantumProgram` generated by `qiskit-mitigation` (or manually constructed), in addition to being able to run a `QuantumProgram` from `qiskit-ibm-runtime`"?

Yes, but after this PR, is there any different using QP from `qiskit-ibm-runtime` vs samplomatic? E.g. do we need to recommend one way or the other in docs?

**What is the expected feature?**

Historically, the test suite of the package has been kept compatible with `unittest`. Re-evaluating the current maturity of `pytest` and the current practices and projects maintained by the team, the team agreed on switching to a `pytest`-style test suite, sacrificing compatibility with other runners and agnosticism in favor of a more convenient usage of `pytest` features and their familiarity.

This story is about moving the test suite to `pytest`, via:
* [x] rewriting `IBMTestCase` (and subclasses) assert-like methods as single functions
* [ ] rewriting `IBMTestCase` (and subclasses) functionality that shapes the subclasses behavior (`setUp` / functions / etc) into `pytest`-like constructs (fixtures, small conventions, markers)
    * [x] unit tests
    * [ ] integration tests
* [ ] remove subtests in favor of parameterizing
* [ ] replacing `ddt` as the mechanism for parametrization in favor of `mark.parametrize`
* [ ] replace asserts
* [ ] convert the actual suite, aiming for a consistent usage of facilities / structure

Ideally, some steps can be taken _before_ converting the suite, prioritizing comfortable easier review. Avoiding having the two styles co-exist would be nice but might not be avoidable (having a specific module be a "guinea pig" for some of the changes might be a sensible option).

Not strictly in scope is for this story is leveraging the full range of `pytest` included fixtures, functions, etc or provide an in-depth optimal usage of fixtures on our side - the goal is to reach a state where the suite is converted, and that we can improve and tune upon.

All the tests in the suite is not based in `unittest`, but in `pytest`.

```python
qc.h(0)
```

issue.title: Improve docs for `num_chunks` argument in the layerwise Richardson extrapolation (LRE) module
issue.body:
In many functions of the layerwise Richardson extrapolation module `mitiq.lre` the docstring says that:

```
num_chunks: Number of desired approximately equal chunks. When the
            number of chunks is the same as the layers in the input circuit,
            the input circuit is unchanged.
```

I think it could be improved since it is a bit unclear and the final sentence is actually wrong.  When the number of chunks is the same as the layers in the input circuit, LRE is applied in its default way and the circuit is changed accordingly.

I write here a simple draft, just to explain what `num_chunks` actually means. Feel free to better re-write.
```
num_chunks: The number of approximately equal-depth circuit chunks.
            Each chunk is treated by LRE as an independent elementary layer, i.e., 
            the smallest unit over which noise is uniformly scaled. The minimum
            value is 1 (reducing to the mitiq.zne technique), and the maximum
            value is the full circuit depth (the default).
```

Remark: `num_chunks` appears in many public and private and functions within `mitiq.lre` . So, if improved, it should be consistently changed everywhere.
